stemMd: A cinema lowered the price of afternoon tickets. More afternoon tickets were sold, but afternoon ticket revenue fell. Which fact best explains both results?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Some patrons attended more than once.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The percentage increase in tickets sold was smaller than the percentage increase in tickets needed to offset the lower price.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The number of screens remained unchanged.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Evening tickets cost more than afternoon tickets.

explanationMd: Revenue is price multiplied by quantity. A lower price can attract more customers while still reducing revenue if the extra quantity is insufficient to compensate for the price reduction.

distractorRationale.e: Evening prices do not explain the change in afternoon revenue.
distractorRationale.c: Refreshment revenue is not ticket revenue.
distractorRationale.d: Capacity remaining constant does not establish the size of the revenue change.
distractorRationale.a: Repeat attendance may increase sales but does not by itself explain lower revenue.
